articles.title: Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park
articles.summary: Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972.
articles.body:
The 40-year-old stormed to a unanimous decision victory to clinch the vacant WBC super-lightweight belt and bow out as a three-time undisputed world champion with 83,000 fans in attendance at Dublin's historic sporting home.

Taylor, an Olympic champion and two-weight undisputed champion, hangs up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest female boxer in history and a game-changing pioneer for women's sport.

It marked the first boxing event to be held at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al "Blue" Lewis on July 19, 1972.

Taylor's win over Pili sees her retire with a professional record of 26-1 having suffered the only blemish of her career in defeat to Chantelle Cameron in May 2023.

"Croke Park, we did it, we brought boxing back to Croke Park," Taylor told DAZN after the fight.

"Every one of you here helped me win. You were with me in London 2012, you got me through the heartbreak of Rio, you stayed with me when I turned pro, you travelled around the world to watch me, now you're here with me.

"I don't know of any other country that would sell 80,000 tickets, Ireland is the only country.

"She was a very awkward opponent and a great opponent. Thank you very much to her for being involved in this epic night."

A night of celebration was capped by a typically-commanding Taylor display, one final clinic of blistering hand speed, elite footwork and ring IQ proving too much for Pili.

Time and time again Taylor unloaded with slick combinations to out-work and out-manoeuvre her French opponent, who struggled to find joy with her counter-shot approach.

As the final round arrived Taylor sought to deliver one closing show, filling the dying seconds with a relentless attack before embracing Pili at the final bell.

It was a fitting, perfect conclusion to a trailblazing career, Taylor not only transforming boxing but asserting herself as perhaps the greatest sportsperson in Irish history.

The Bray Bomber has been instrumental in catapulting women's boxing in prominence on the modern sporting landscape, paving the way for a thriving female fighting scene.

Taylor became Ireland's first female Olympic boxing champion at London 2012 when she beat Russia's Sofya Ochigava in the lightweight gold medal bout.

She turned professional in 2016 after compiling an amateur record of 176-12-1 before becoming the WBA lightweight world champion in just her seventh contest.

In June 2019 she became undisputed lightweight world champion after defeating Delfine Persoon by majority decision at Madison Square Garden.

Taylor returned to make history at the MSG three years later as she and Puerto Rican great Amanda Serrano staged the first ever women's boxing fight to headline at the iconic New York venue. It would mark the beginning of a landmark trilogy between the pair, Taylor winning on all three occasions.

Her first career defeat arrived in May 2023 when she stepped up to super-lightweight to face Cameron, losing by majority decision before winning the rematch with the same outcome six months later to become a two-weight undisputed champion.

In the moments that followed her final hand-raise Taylor afforded herself a moment to look around and absorb the sight of a stunning sold-out Croke Park, before being serenaded again by a roar that barely faded all evening.

As is boxing tradition, she would then lay down her gloves in the middle of the ring before members of her team followed with each of her six championship belts, a lap of honour following as she said her final goodbye.

articles.title: Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash
articles.summary: A long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the proposed clash in November; Fury called out Oleksandr Usyk on Monday
articles.body:
With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent.

Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024.

Responding to Fury's comments in a statement given to Sky Sports News on Monday evening, Usyk's manager Sergey Lapin said: "Usyk is not Tyson's backup plan.

"If Fury needs an opponent, he should visit the Ready to Fight platform . They can help him find a worthy opponent there.

"Oleksandr is always open to big challenges. But serious intentions are backed by a concrete offer, not statements in the press."

Usyk announced in June that he was vacating the three heavyweight belts he still held at the time, but the 39-year-old said he was not yet retiring, and has recently been linked with a fight against Deontay Wilder.

Usyk, who holds a perfect 25-0 professional record, claimed successive wins over Joshua in 2021 and 2022, but has become part of the Brit's training team over the last year.

Both Joshua and Fury have signed individual contracts for what was slated to be a November contest, but have yet to agree on where the fight will take place, with speculation suggesting it could be held in New York City.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says he and his fighter want the contest to take place in London, while Fury says his rival is trying to avoid a bout that has been more than a decade in the making.

"This will only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk," Fury said in a video posted on Instagram .

"Oleksandr you're his [Joshua's] trainer and his sensei and you know he is weak minded... and that he would never fight the Gypsy King which you have had the guts to do twice.

"You got the decisions last time, fair play to you. Good luck to you, let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court... do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits?

"Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent."

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is less and less likely to happen, says Johnny Nelson
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's all-British blockbuster fight has been stuck in negotiations in recent months, but Eddie Hearn revealed last week that talks have 'reopened' to stage the fight at Wembley
articles.body:
Promoter Eddie Hearn has stated that Joshua signed a contract to fight Fury at Wembley amid an ongoing dispute over the location of the fight, with Madison Square Garden in New York also being considered as a potential venue.

Nelson believes Joshua and his team are even more determined to get the fight entirely on their terms after the unified champion displayed his vulnerabilities while being floored twice in his comeback win over Kristian Prenga .

"No, I don't [think Fury vs Joshua will happen]," Nelson told Sky Sports.

"Unless the other side decides to lay down and say: 'You know what, we'll give you what you want'. No, I don't.

"I think Anthony Joshua and [his promotional team] Matchroom Boxing have every reason to stand their ground.

"Firstly, because you look at Anthony Joshua's last performance; that doesn't fill you with confidence.

"Secondly, because they've signed a contract and so, if they're going to embark on this fight, they're going to say: 'This is what we asked for; if you don't want to do it, that's a you problem'."

Hearn has revealed that he held fresh talks with London Mayor Sadiq Khan in a bid to ensure the two Brits fight in front of a home crowd, despite concerns over a later curfew for Wembley Stadium.

But Nelson believes Joshua and his team's insistence that the terms of the contract should be followed could mean the bout is not agreed.

"I think it's less and less likely to happen," said Nelson.

"They have put the pressure on. Sadiq Khan has got involved, and he's said: 'We're going to do everything possible to make this happen and bring this business to the UK'.

"Anthony Joshua has said to Eddie Hearn, 'We've got a contract; stick to the contract. No nudging; this is what we're doing.

"Unless Turki Alalshikh [who is organising the fight] and Tyson [Fury], say: 'All right, let's do this.'

"I think that the chance of the fight happening is less and less.

"If I were Team AJ, I'd do the same, because AJ's performance didn't fill me with complete and utter belief that this will go our way.

"I'm quite sure if it was the other way around and Tyson Fury was the one who performed as AJ did in his last fight, even though he fought the night before, I'm quite sure this wouldn't be as much of an issue.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua car crash: Trial of driver involved in fatal collision has hearing adjourned until November 17
articles.summary: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode was driving an SUV that struck a stationary truck on December 29 2025, injuring Anthony Joshua and killing two members of his team; He is facing a four-count charge
articles.body:
The case, which began in January at a magistrate court in Ogun State, was adjourned from September 10 as proceedings continued over charges arising from the fatal crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach, Sina Ghami, were killed.

Kayode faces charges including dangerous driving causing death, reckless and negligent driving, driving without due care and attention, and operating a vehicle without a valid national driver's licence.

The 46-year-old Kayode denies the charges.

Prosecutors allege that Kayode was attempting to overtake another vehicle when the SUV carrying Joshua and his team crashed into a stationary truck.

Joshua, a two-time world heavyweight champion, survived injuries he sustained in the crash in December last year and was later discharged.

The crash occurred as the group was traveling to visit Joshua's father in Ogun State.

Police told the court in earlier proceedings that both vehicles had been removed from the scene before investigators arrived.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn in latest war of words as Teofimo Lopez gatecrashes press conference in disguise
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia accused Conor Benn of struggling to make weight while the Brit insisted he was "not here for a cuddle" as the pair traded blows at their final press conference ahead of Saturday night's WBC welterweight world title fight in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
WBC welterweight champion Garcia (25-2, 20 KOs) is set to defend his title for the first time against Benn after clinching the belt against Mario Barrios in February.

Benn (25-1, 14 KOs) meanwhile steps into comfortably the biggest test of his career on the back of April's win over Regis Prograis and his revenge victory over Chris Eubank Jr.

"Just don't cuddle me in here. I didn't come all the way to America for you to cuddle," said Benn.

Both fighters have previously being caught up in controversy with Garcia testing positive for banned substance ostarine in 2024, while in the same year Benn's provisional anti-doping suspension for two failed drugs test in 2022 was lifted.

Garcia, who was a no-show for Wednesday's face-off, was the more animated of the two fighters as he fired insults across the table towards the Brit.

The American's talking continued during the pair's face-off, to which Benn simply raised his finger to his lips before exiting the stage.

"He's going to try real hard, we know that. He's probably going to have to try to resort to some dirty tactics, so we'll be prepared for that," said Garcia.

"And we're just going to do what we do best, which is stay sharp, be ready for everything, and we're prepared, man. We're conditioned 100 percent, and we'll put on a hell of a show, I promise you that."

Benn is making a significant cut in weight having twice fought Eubank Jr at middleweight, his last fight at the 10st 7lb welterweight limit coming against Chris van Heerden in April 2022.

Saturday awaits as the 29-year-old's first-ever world title fight and toughest opponent by some distance.

"I'm not concerned," said Benn. "I don't focus on him and what he does, I focus on what I do. I bring tenacity, ferocity, spite, experience. I've been here before, I've fought in front of 70,000 three times now, on the bounce. So you know I'm here to come and really set the tone from the first round."

Among his barrage of insults, Garcia again questioned Benn's weigh-cut, suggesting he would struggle on the scales the next day.

"I know you're not on weight, because I can see it in your eyes. You ain't on weight," he said. "Hey, you're going to hit that bathtub tonight, or the bike."

Garcia took particular offense to Benn questioning his Mexican heritage, while also firing back at his opponent's father Nigel Benn.

"Come Saturday night when his blood is spilling out his mouth, that will be enough to show him how Mexican I am," he said.

"I heard his dad talking like he was gonna knock me out. Bet he won't. Bet he won't. We can bet whatever too. Your son ain't gonna knock me out. He couldn't even knock out Regis. Your dad ain't right. Your dad lying to you. I hope you know that. Dad lying to you."

Benn insisted Garcia should "worry about himself".

"He seems to have enough problems as it is," he said.

"I don't look at him, I just worry about myself and don't cut corners. We'll see who makes weight tomorrow."

Another twist to their press conference was a surprise appearance by WBA 'Super' welterweight world champion Lopez, who wore a fake beard and introduced himself as 'Jack Hoffman' as he asked a question in the crowd.

articles.title: Conor Benn's 'graduation day' is here but Ryan Garcia could be a class above in Las Vegas clash, says Johnny Nelson
articles.summary: Conor Benn will challenge Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight title at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas in the early hours of Sunday morning; Sky Sports expert Johnny Nelson is refusing to write off the British fighter who is challenging for his first world title
articles.body:
Benn will challenge for his first world title when he takes on Garcia for the WBC welterweight belt at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas in the early hours of Sunday morning.

The Californian floored and outpointed Mario Barrios to become the new WBC champion in February, while he has previously fought elite champions such as Devin Haney and Gervonta Davis.

But Nelson is refusing to rule out a stunning victory for Benn.

"Never say never," Nelson told Sky Sports. "Right now, it seems like an impossible mountain to climb, because Conor Benn hasn't answered the questions that needed answering. Has he got that depth of experience? He hasn't. Can he dig deep? We know he can. Is he that level of a fighter? That's a question we don't know the answer to.

"What we do know is, historically, this has happened time and time again before. Lloyd Honeyghan going over to America and winning the world title shocked everybody. Conor's dad, Nigel Benn, going over and beating Iran Barkley. You know, Barkley had a bit of a name for himself; could Nigel do it? He did do it, and he did it after getting knocked out by Michael Watson.

"So, because the style is probably so crude and rugged, you'd think, has this kid [Conor Benn] got the class to become a world champion and be, what looks like, a class act?

"It just has to be his night. Obviously, you'd understand people leaning towards Ryan Garcia because Garcia is proven. Conor isn't. So you're going to give a man a chance to prove himself, not write him off."

Benn stepped up to middleweight to settle his rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr, losing the first fight on points before avenging the defeat with a dominant victory on the scorecards in the rematch.

The 29-year-old endured a tough weight cut to drop down towards 147lbs for the Garcia fight, but Nelson insists the all-action Brit will be a 'machine' in the ring.

"I don't believe the weight will take away his armoury," said Nelson. "It will obviously take away the natural strength that he had at a higher weight.

"He won't be completely depleted. I think he'll still be a machine. He'll be faster. He'll not be stronger. I think he'll have the speed, but not have the strength that he showed when we saw him box Eubank Jr.

"I think speed creates power, and the attrition, the number of shots that he throws, they are blistering.

"We've seen him take people out before; we've seen him concussively take people out.

"But I think speed creates power, and it's navigating that. It's about how he goes about that."

Benn floored Eubank Jr twice in their second fight, while he also demolished former world champion Chris Algieri, but Nelson believes Garcia will be a far more challenging proposition.

"This is graduation day for Conor Benn," said Nelson. "I expect Garcia to be a class above. I expect Garcia to take Conor seriously, and I expect him to go out and be fast and be sharp and be dominant.

"So, this is for Ryan Garcia to lose because if there's any scent of arrogance, complacency, or dismissiveness from him in regard to Conor, that will be his reckoning. That will be his downfall.

"This is one of those fights where you've got to be on your A-game. Ryan Garcia has to go in there and respect Conor. What I've seen and what I've heard doesn't tell me that; he thinks this is easy work.

"This might be just talk. It might be fighting talk, but I hope he's taking Conor seriously because if he hasn't, he's giving a man a chance who, on paper, shouldn't have one."

articles.title: Ryan Garcia finishes Conor Benn in just two rounds to defend WBC welterweight world championship in Las Vegas
articles.summary: Conor Benn moved back to welterweight to challenger American star Ryan Garcia for the WBC world championship at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas; Garcia overwhelmed Benn with a stunning onslaught in the second round to defend his title
articles.body:
Garcia successfully defended the WBC welterweight championship with a ruthless display of speed, power and precision, ending Benn's world title dream early in their Las Vegas showdown.

Benn was stepping up to a new level in the first world title fight of his career as the UK star attempted to secure what would have been one of British boxing's biggest overseas upsets.

Benn was fighting below the welterweight limit for the first time in over four years.

Last year, after his provisional suspension for an anti-doping violation was lifted, Benn boxed family rival Chris Eubank Jr twice at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Both of those bouts were up at middleweight, with Benn avenging his loss in the first contest when he dropped and outscored Eubank in the second.

He began moving back down to welterweight after that, meeting Regis Prograis in a catchweight bout, also at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, on the undercard of Tyson Fury's comeback earlier this year.

He completed the challenge of boiling back down in weight but couldn't match Garcia.

In his career Garcia has come up from lighter divisions, but has mixed in exalted company. He recorded a stunning win over Olympic gold medallist Luke Campbell and lost to Gervonta Davis at lightweight. He dominated Devin Haney, although he came in over the super-lightweight limit for that fight. That result was changed to a no contest after Garcia failed a drug test.

After a year-long ban, he lost to Rolando Romero in a Times Square event before getting a shot at then WBC champion Mario Barrios. Garcia dropped Barrios en route to winning a decision and claiming the belt.

Benn was installed as his mandatory challenger but Garcia showed his calibre early on the fight. At the outset he shook up the Briton with a quick left hook.

At the end of the first round Garcia unleashed hurtful back hands, while Benn tried to club back at him with his right.

In the second round Garcia ripped his right across to drop Benn heavily. The Briton rose unsteadily. He needed to clinch to try to clear his head, but the American pinned him on the end of savage punches.

Garcia tore into him, smashing him into the ropes. He hurt Benn to the body and then battered him round the head, his sheer speed clearly apparent. The referee then stepped between them to end it at 1:25 of the second round.

"I kind of figured he would just come at me crazy," Garcia said.

"Second round, I said I'm tired of him coming forward; I'm going stand my ground a little bit ... and then he got caught with a hellacious one."

On the undercard Australia's formidable cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia continued his unbeaten run, dispatching WBC titlist Noel Mikaelian.

In the ninth round the southpaw cracked Mikaelian with a left hook then an even harder right hook, leaving him stunned on the ropes. The strands held him up so the referee administered a count but Mikaelian could not continue from there and was stopped at 1:30 of the session.

articles.title: Conor Benn confronts his future options after crushing loss to Ryan Garcia: 'What next? I don't have the answer'
articles.summary: Conor Benn lost his bid for the WBC welterweight world title inside two crushing rounds when he fought Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas; Benn is left considering his next options but says: "The truth is, I don't have the answer"; Moving back to middleweight is a likely route for him
articles.body:
Benn was attempting to follow in his famous father Nigel's footsteps and become a world champion when he challenged Garcia for the WBC belt at the T-Mobile Arena.

But Garcia, a top-class fighter, handed Benn a crushing loss when he dropped and stopped him in their second round.

"Everybody keeps asking: 'What's next for Conor Benn?'" he stated on social media. "The truth is, I don't have the answer.

"If you'd asked the 19-year-old version of me whether I thought I'd be standing here 10 years later, having lived through everything I have, I'd have told you that you were crazy.

"I train hard. I sacrifice. I've given this game 110 per cent every time I've stepped through those ropes, I've wanted to give people unforgettable nights and entertain.

"That's what this has always been about for me.

"People spend their hard-earned money to come and watch guys like us fight. I've never taken that for granted. I've always wanted to be a servant of the public and give everything I have when it matters."

The signs are that he will rest, recover and take some time out before considering how to return.

"Giving everything comes at a cost," he continued. "And the people who have paid that cost more than anyone are my family and my kids.

"They've sacrificed time with their dad so I could chase this dream. They've had to share me with this sport their entire lives.

"So when people ask me what's next for Conor Benn, right now the answer is simple.

He added: "Fight fans, thank you. Those who travelled to Vegas, those who stayed up until the early hours. I will never take your support for granted, especially on those nights things don't go to plan."

Benn is only 29 years old, so while he might take some time out of boxing, he can be expected to return to the sport.

The bout with Garcia was his first fight at welterweight in over four years. After two middleweight bouts with Chris Eubank Jr, the drop back to 147lbs was severe.

All the indications are that Benn will seek to go back up in weight. He could bypass 154lbs altogether and bounce back to middleweight.

There are title belt holders at 160lbs who have championships but relatively low profiles. Aaron McKenna, the IBF champion, and Denzel Bentley, now the WBO titleholder, for instance would surely welcome a fight with Benn if he could get ranked.

Perhaps he could move even higher in weight, even though he'd be small at middleweight let alone super-middle. But having a trilogy bout with Eubank Jr at 168lbs could make sense. It would save Eubank the punishing weight cut he had at middleweight with a rehydration clause and the two are 1-1 in their series.

For Benn, his Las Vegas adventure ended in a crushing defeat to Garcia, but there will be options for him as and when he chooses to return.

articles.title: Tom Aspinall vacates UFC heavyweight championship as he seeks to recover from on-going eye issues
articles.summary: Tom Aspinall has announced that he will vacate the UFC heavyweight title; Aspinall hasn't fought since October 2025 when his defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no contest after he was poked in the eyes; Aspinall is still trying to recover from his injuries
articles.body:
Britain's Aspinall hasn't fought since October 2025 when his defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no contest due to an eye poke.

Aspinall has had multiple medical procedures to address ongoing issues with his eyes since then but is still not ready to return to competition.

He has decided to vacate his title in the meantime.

"Ongoing eye complications mean I cannot get cleared to fight right now," Aspinall said. "I've had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing.

"I know there has been questions about why I have been quiet. I have always followed the advice of the UFC and focused on my recovery while we've tried to make this happen.

"I have now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don't want to hold the heavyweight division up.

"I know what it's like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title."

He added: "We have worked closely with different doctors and specialists to try and make my return happen but, unfortunately, it is simply not possible right now.

"I am absolutely gutted. I have chased this dream since I was 10 years old."

articles.title: Conor Benn comeback? WBO champion Denzel Bentley says Conor Benn can 'skip the queue' for middleweight world title shot
articles.summary: Conor Benn suffered a devastating two-round defeat in Las Vegas when he challenged Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight world title at the weekend; but Benn could now return to middleweight and WBO 160lb world champion Denzel Bentley has offered him a shot at his title
articles.body:
Denzel Bentley, the WBO world champion at 160lbs, is open to fighting Benn.

Benn twice boxed his family rival, Chris Eubank Jr, at middleweight before boiling back down to welterweight to challenge Ryan Garcia for the WBC title.

Garcia hammered Benn inside two rounds, with Benn now expected to return to middleweight.

Bentley, elevated to full world champion after claiming the WBO interim title with a storming performance against Endry Saavedra in April, would relish the prospect of defending his belt against Benn.

"Although the public might not think he deserves another world title shot in my eyes I feel like his profile is big enough for him to skip the queue," Bentley told Sky Sports .

"It's unfair but that's the sport we're in. Obviously it's beneficial for me, especially financially, so 100 per cent that's the fight I would take. I've never had any beef with Conor, we've always been cool.

"But if he is coming to the 160lb division, he goes from a companion to a potential challenger," he added.

"Firstly he needs to get himself right, well and fit. I think he should take a lot of time off and recover. I don't think there's any rush for him to get back into a boxing ring or even a gym. That weight cut was a fight in itself for him I think. Probably took a lot out of himself.

"Once he's well and fit, if he decides to move up to 160lbs and he does want the challenge, I think that's probably a conversation we can probably have ourselves: 'If you want to do this, let's push for it.'"

Bentley though had a warning for him. "I think I'm dangerous for anyone. I'm a lot bigger than him and I can punch."

But he added: "I think he will be a lot better with the extra weight.

"I think at 160lbs he'll be a lot more fuelled. But, listen, I punch as well and there were a lot of flaws in his game that night that I could exploit."

articles.title: James DeGale admits George Groves rivalry still makes him 'cringe' as he prepares for his comeback
articles.summary: James DeGale says his heated dispute with George Groves on Sky Sports show 'Ringside' is 'part of my journey'; the former world champion returns to the ring this month against Marcus Portman; DeGale has urged Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua to finally agree a lucrative 'farewell' fight
articles.body:
DeGale had an entertaining war of words with his fellow Londoner before they settled their dispute in a 2011 grudge fight as Groves emerged victorious by split decision at The O2 Arena.

Despite this early setback, DeGale would go on to become a two-time world super-middleweight champion, although the 40-year-old is still regularly reminded about his lively dispute with Groves on Sky Sports show 'Ringside.'

Speaking to Dev Sahni, Groves said: "It's a classic. I cringe when I watch that [clip of himself and Groves], but it's a classic.

"That's me at the age of 25. Brash, cocky, [wearing] Dolce and Gabbana.

"It's raw, thinking I was the man, but that's just a part of my journey."

DeGale defeated Andre Dirrell to secure the IBF title in Boston in 2015, while he also defeated Lucian Bute in Quebec and then battled to a thrilling draw with Badou Jack in New York.

But the Olympic gold medallist fears he is only remembered for losses against Groves and Chris Eubank Jnr on British soil.

"That Groves one was close. I can't argue. A lot of people thought I won. A lot of people thought he won," said DeGale.

"And then the Eubank one was just a mess.

"That's probably why the fans don't see me as one of the best, because of my losses against British opponents, but they don't realise that I had better wins than them.

"Let's be real, [Andre] Dirrell, was a quality amateur. He beat Carl Froch but didn't get the decision, it was close though. He was a bronze medallist in the Olympic Games, he would have beaten George and Chris.

"Bute had like 13 title defences. I had the war with Badou Jack. Even before that, [Marco Antonio] Periban, [Rogelio] Medina [Luna], Brandon Gonzalez."

DeGale is returning from retirement to face Marcus Portman in Wolverhampton on September 26, over seven years since his last fight against Eubank in which he says injuries severely hampered his performance.

Britain's current biggest rivalry between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could finally be settled in December, with The Principality Stadium in Cardiff and Wembley Stadium being considered as potential venues.

"It's egos, boxing politics. I'm not too sure, it's a bit of a mess," said DeGale when asked about the Fury vs Joshua saga.

"You would think it would be in England, a nice farewell for AJ and Fury.

"It looks like they are coming to the end now.

"Get a £100m each and then run, say 'thank you, you've been brilliant, and then later.'"

articles.title: Amy Broadhurst continues comeback at European championships: 'This will be my last shot at the Olympics'
articles.summary: Amy Broadhurst is continuing her boxing comeback after becoming a mother; A World and European gold medallist for Ireland, Broadhurst has switched to GB and will box for Britain at the European Championships, her first major tournament since having a baby
articles.body:
Amy Broadhurst, a former World and European gold medallist for Ireland, will be part of the squad boxing for Britain.

Broadhurst, a key sparring partner for Katie Taylor for the Irish legend's first iconic victory over Amanda Serrano, switched from Ireland to Britain ahead of Paris 2024 as she sought to qualify for the Olympic Games.

These European championships will be her first major championships since returning to competition after the birth of her baby boy.

"It's tough but we're making it work and I'm very lucky to have the support around me," Broadhurst told Sky Sports . "He's at the right age now where this is possible.

"He'll come to Bulgaria with me and he comes to Sheffield every second week with me," she continued. "Those weeks are tough because you're doing two jobs then.

"This is my last shot at the Olympics. So they know after this it's all said and done."

These Europeans will be a key step on a journey that she hopes will eventually take her to LA 2028. But her return to boxing has already been eventful. The first bout in her comeback earlier this year saw her drawn against her old team.

"My first fight back after two years was against Ireland. So that was a mad situation," she said.

"I was trying to control my feelings because obviously a lot of [stuff] went on with that whole situation.

"I knew going in that I was going to do okay. But there was just a lot of ill feelings on both behalfs. I think I handled it very well. I shook hands with the coach and I showed respect. That was probably the main thing, not to get sucked into the emotional part of it. It was get in, box and move on. It was like closing the chapter on something. We shook hands and then that's it."

She didn't box Ireland's top lightweight then but that could potentially happen in Sofia. Kellie Harrington, Ireland's two-time Olympic champion, has entered these Europeans.

"I was her sparring partner for the 2021 Games," Broadhurst said. "I was brought over to Tokyo.

"We've shared the ring many times and it would be a spicy fight.

"You could meet each other," Broadhurst noted. "You just don't know what's going to happen.

Richards fights Belgrade's Radivoje Kalajdzic in the chief support to Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton.

"I think going out there and putting on a statement performance against him puts my name in a hat for that world title, 100 per cent," Richards told Sky Sports . "I'm locked in. I'm ready to do a job.

In 2021, Richards challenged Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title, losing on a unanimous but closer than expected decision. Bivol subsequently established himself as the best in the division when he beat Beterbiev.

That is the level Richards wants to get back to.

articles.title: Johnny Fisher: Michael Pirotton pledges September 26 Copper Box upset | 'His mind is broke. Too much pressure!'
articles.summary: Watch Johnny Fisher fight Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena on September 26, live on Sky Sports; Belgium's Pirotton is convinced that he will beat Fisher in London: "I know his mind is broke and he's facing too much pressure for himself"
articles.body:
The Belgian heavyweight will travel to London to box popular puncher Fisher at the Copper Box Arena, live on Sky Sports .

He knows he will be lightly regarded. Pirotton has been defeated twice before and Fisher is a high-profile name in the division.

"I'm the exact opposite," Pirotton told Sky Sports . "He has the best promotion, the best trainers since the beginning and all that and I've been doing it my own way since the beginning. I had to go through the dirty part of the business."

But he is adamant that underrating him is a perilous mistake. Fisher himself is far from invincible. He has not won on UK soil for over two years. He struggled with Dave Allen and then was stopped by him in their rematch. Fisher was clipped and seemingly buzzed too in his most recent victory over Ivan Balaz in December.

Pirotton has never been dropped or stopped.

"I took two losses. I know the losses were meaningful to become the man I am today. I know these losses came from outside the ring, not really inside. Maybe if I didn't have those setbacks I wouldn't be able to believe in myself so deeply like I am now," the Belgian insisted.

"I think that's how I'm going to prevail over my opponent on the 26th. Because I know his mind is broke and he's facing too much pressure for himself. He can act tough and cocky and all that but he's never been through what I've been through.

"I've been broken, broken, broken again and still I rose. I'm still here. I know people don't know me. It would be naive for a guy like me to hope people won't make fun of me."

He has noted online jibes, which even prompted him to find out what Piriton, the hayfever medication was.

"I had to accept fights when I was not ready or barely training because I had to work," said Pirotton, who is priced at around 7/1 to win by bookmakers.

"Guess what, some of us are plumbers, some of us are doormen. Guess what, I've been working as a doorman at night and training in the day. People make fun of you, but it's my price to be able to keep living the dream.

"The way to beat Johnny is to outsmart the guy. I think people won't rate my boxing IQ because honestly I've never shown it properly, except in a few fights and sparring and all that.

"I've never been on such a big stage. But I know my quality. I'm ready to be embracing the moment and just be me and risk it all.

"For all the plumbers just bet on me, I see I have great odds… This is for you!"

articles.title: Isaac Okoh: Commonwealth Games gold medallist begins European Championship campaign | 'I can beat anyone in the world'
articles.summary: The European Boxing Championships are under way in Sofia, Bulgaria; Great Britain has a strong team in the competition with heavyweight Isaac Okoh looking to continue his winning run when he has his first bout in the event on Sunday; Okoh is the Commonwealth Games gold medallist
articles.body:
After underwhelming at the World Championships a year ago, Okoh has been on a fantastic winning run which culminated in a Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow.

He now wants to keep the momentum rolling into the European Championships, which are under way in Sofia.

Okoh has his first bout in Bulgaria on Sunday against Poland's Alexey Sevostyanov.

"I'm confident I can beat anyone in the world at the minute. It's going to take a really good fighter to beat me," Okoh told Sky Sports .

"There's a lot of great competitors at the weight. I feel like I'm up there and I'm in real contention for a gold medal.

"I'm well up for it and I fancy my chances against anyone at this tournament."

His victory in Glasgow has buoyed that confidence. "It's a dream come true, When you first start boxing the Commonwealth Games is one of the tournaments you dream of going to and then obviously to bring home the gold medal not too far away from home with friends and family there, it's a proud moment," Okoh said.

"It fills you with confidence going on into the future, Olympic qualifiers round the corner and the Olympics two years away.

"Since the World championships I've been boxing brilliantly. I knew I had to… I've been flying."

Britain has a strong team at these European championships.

"We've got a great squad. We had a brilliant medal tally coming back from the Commonwealths, one of the best in a long time. We've got a great squad at the minute, lots of talent, very young, fresh, hungry. So the mood's brilliant in camp and morale's through the roof," Okoh said.

"It's a great team and a great group of people to be around."

Although Sacha Hickey suffered a surprise loss to Croatia's Sara Beram, fellow Commonwealth Games medallist Ruby White got off to a strong start.

After losing in the flyweight final in Glasgow, White returned to action on Saturday and dominated Serbia's Nikolina Dzida, handing her counts in the first and second rounds en route to taking a clear unanimous decision.

articles.title: Pat Brown delivers Ricky Hatton tribute after winning British and Commonwealth titles as Isaac Cruz calls out Ryan Garcia
articles.summary: Pat Brown paid tribute to Ricky Hatton after beating John Hedges to take the vacant British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles in only his seventh professional fight; Isaac Cruz called out Ryan Garcia after retaining his WBC interim super-lightweight title in San Diego
articles.body:
The 26-year-old Olympian took his professional record to seven wins from seven, every one inside the distance, adding the Lonsdale Belt to the WBA International and IBF Intercontinental titles already in his possession.

For Hedges, it was a case of unlucky number 13 after the Harlow-born fighter had gone unbeaten through his first 12 fights.

It was anything but straightforward for Brown, though. Hedges is 6ft 6in, and a southpaw, and the 24-year-old spent the opening exchanges making himself hard to hit, giving Brown nothing to aim at and grabbing hold whenever the Mancunian worked his way inside.

Frustration began to build for Brown and he started leaning on Hedges with his head and forcing him back over the top rope until referee Reece Carter intervened.

Something appeared to click in the fifth for Brown as he stopped hunting for one shot, put the jab to work and landed a right uppercut flush under the chin. Then, having aimed high for five rounds, he went to the ribs in the sixth.

A strong hook downstairs folded Hedges on to one knee and after he got to his feet, a second body shot moments later saw him downed and unable to get back up as Brown sealed an emotional and meaningful victory which he dedicated to British boxing legend Ricky Hatton, who tragically passed away a year and five days prior to the fight.

Brown said: "I finished him with a body shot in memory of him."

Both fighters had strong connections to Hatton, with Brown sharing a gym with the former welterweight world champion - who also trained Hedges, taking him to the English title.

Brown was given strong support throughout from a large travelling contingent from his native Sale, with fans chanting his name from the first bell.

"I can't just go bulldozing in with him, people think you can't box," he explained on DAZN . "With John, you're not going to get him out of there straight away because he'll just make you miss and make you look silly.

"That's why it was a patient performance."

On the undercard, Shabaz Masoud shut out Ckari Mansilla 100-90 on all three cards to take the WBA International and IBF Intercontinental featherweight titles.

Elsewhere, Mark Jeffers outpointed Kieron Conway in a British super-middleweight eliminator and Cory O'Regan became English lightweight champion at the expense of Joe Howarth.

Cruz calls out Garcia after stopping Bravo

Isaac Cruz has called out Ryan Garcia after knocking out Nestor Bravo in San Diego to retain his WBC interim super-lightweight title for a second time at the Pechanga Arena in a controversial contest.

"Hey, Ryan, I'm here," Cruz, known by the nickname 'Pitbull', said after winning the fight. "My next fight for you. Come on, Ryan."

By Monday he was talking about a fast turnaround, naming December or January for his return and Cruz among the men he would face.

Whether it is that simple is another matter as Garcia has also been linked with a fight against Teofimo Lopez, who holds a world title at welterweight, while Cruz operates a division below.

Garcia responded to callout following the fight, though, and said: "Pitbull proved me wrong tonight. Let's do this in December, the offer is on the table.

"I can tame a lion, I'm not to concerned about taming a pitbull."

On Saturday night though, Cruz boxed effectively and started fast as he caught Bravo with a hook in the first round as the Puerto Rican attempted to tie up.

Then came the controversy, courtesy of the referee.

Thomas Taylor took a point off Bravo in the second for holding, warned both men in the third after a series of low blows and docked the Puerto Rican again in the fourth for dumping Cruz on the canvas - telling him bluntly that a disqualification would leave him unpaid.

The fight ended in the sixth as a lead left hook landed clean midway through the round, knocking Bravo to the canvas as he lost for just the second time in his career, while Cruz moves to 29-3-2.

Daniel Blancas, Marco Verde and Eumir Marcial all won inside the distance on the undercard.

articles.title: Conor Benn and Moses Itauma: Former champion George Groves on how they should rebuild after 'mental scarring' of defeat
articles.summary: George Groves considers how Moses Itauma and Conor Benn should now rebuild after their world championship fight defeats; Watch Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton on Saturday September 26 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Both were halted in their first world title fights. Ryan Garcia savagely ended Benn's challenge for the WBC welterweight belt in just two rounds, while Itauma crumbled in the ninth round when boxing Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF strap.

George Groves became a big name in British boxing but was no stranger to adversity in his career - it took him four attempts to win a world championship.

He says Itauma, who is still only 21 years old, must demonstrate his resolve.

"He's going to have to show a lot of resilience to come back from that as well as remain confident with self-belief," Groves told Sky Sports .

"There's no way you can train to that level of exhaustion. It's not like you can go into the gym and replicate that. It's never going to be, in the gym, as important as what it is - a world title fight at his age underneath the lights with everything on the line.

"He's been there now and that's a credit to him… Now you've got to use that.

"It's not an easy task but I hope that there isn't a lot of mental scarring there and they can go back and not try and reinvent. Keep what he is but just give him more comfort and confidence in the pacing of the fight."

That's something Itauma will have to learn.

"Maybe it will come with age, that endurance that he can be much more of a 12 round fighter than a three-round fighter. At the moment he's a three-round fighter. That's the sad fact of it. He's not even a six-round fighter. I thought he was gassing a bit from the third round on," Groves said.

"He's that sort of athlete, extremely fast twitch and when he punches he puts maximum effort into it. But that depletes the engine. At times he's probably never really had to work on it.

"But he's going to have to be much more efficient in his work."

Groves does think Itauma needs to regroup against an easier opponent.

"If I had to rebuild Moses Itauma. I would drop him obviously down a level but I've got to be honest I think his management has been great so far. I'm not buying into 'the Hrgovic fight was a step too far'. It was what it was. It was the right fight to make. It got elevated to a world title," he said.

"It was logical to elevate it to a world title and with that maybe came some pressure. Moses, he probably thought he had Hrgovic gone and he didn't and put his foot on the gas a bit too much and he gassed out. So he's going to have to own that a little bit. They'll change and adapt within his training team to patch that up.

"Get him in with someone durable, someone not as durable as Hrgovic maybe."

But Groves added: "The Hrgovic fight, it was the right fight to have.

"Hrgovic is good, he's been about, he's tough but in some ways he's made for Itauma because, although he's big and strong, he's not quick. He had nothing in that fight. The only time he has success was when Itauma just came away from his boxing style because he was exhausted," the former champion explained.

"The toughest job in boxing is probably navigating Itauma's career because he's been so good, so fast, so early, so young."

Conor Benn also faces a tricky rebuilding job. He moved up in weight for two 160lb clashes with Chris Eubank Jr last year, worked his way back to welter for Garcia but then came unstuck.

"I'm not sure where he lies at true world class," Groves said. "If he's not going to stay at 147lbs, who can he beat at 154lbs and who can he beat at 160lbs?

"I don't think [middleweight] is a good move. I'd go up to 154, I know that's a tough division with loads of really good fighters who aren't necessarily the massive marquee names.

"Maybe another camp at 147 could be good. But then you're in with Teofimo Lopez, Shakur Stevenson."

Benn will likely consider completing a trilogy with Eubank Jr, potentially at super-middleweight.

Groves said: "Hopefully it's not all roads lead to Eubank because I think that's done. That rivalry is done. I've got a feeling that's what it will be.

"I'm not a huge fan of that but that's probably the best of Conor Benn's options."

Benn has already had a number of lucrative fights. But he's not expected to call it a day there.

"He's made crazy money but I don't think he'll retire," Groves noted. "I don't think he'd want to retire off the back of that loss and he definitely won't walk away from the table when there's still food there."

articles.title: “That's crazy”: Fans left amazed as Arman Tsarukyan predicted his Mauricio Ruffy elbow KO a month before UFC 331 fight
articles.summary: MMA News: Arman Tsarukyan produced one of the most spectacular finishes of UFC 331 when he knocked out Mauricio Ruffy with a pair of elbows. But the stunning fi.
articles.body: Arman Tsarukyan produced one of the most spectacular finishes of UFC 331 when he knocked out Mauricio Ruffy with a pair of elbows. But the stunning finish was not completely unexpected. Weeks before stepping into the Octagon, Tsarukyan had already spoken about using elbows to stop the dangerous Brazilian striker.His prediction was not exact, as he expected the finish to come in the third round. The actual knockout came much earlier, with just four seconds left in the opening round at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.Arman Tsarukyan saw the elbow finish coming at UFC 331Arman Tsarukyan had predicted a third-round TKO involving elbows during an appearance with streamer N3on. He said, “Round 3 stoppage via TKO. Elbows, elbows - cut his face.” What followed at UFC 331 was remarkably similar in style, only much quicker and more devastating. Tsarukyan trapped Ruffy against the cage before landing a clean elbow that sent him down. A second elbow followed as the referee stopped the fight.The prediction became even more interesting after the fight.Fans couldn't keep calm on social media as the clip of his prediction went viral. One fan wrote, “hmm wonder if he was being serious in this video”, another added, “He studied tape and probably practiced it”. One commented, “Ruffy was too focused on wrestling forgot Arman isn’t just a cr*tch sniffer”, while another wrote, “W arman he called it!! Crazy how he was with n3on and predicted it”. A user wrote, “That’s crazy”.Tsarukyan entered UFC 331 with a reputation as one of the best wrestlers in the lightweight division. Ruffy, meanwhile, was known for his dangerous striking. Many expected Tsarukyan to rely heavily on his grappling to control the Brazilian.Instead, he found his biggest moment with a strike. Ruffy was able to defend Tsarukyan’s early attempts to take him down. The Armenian then used his clinch work to keep Ruffy against the cage. With the Brazilian fighting for position, Tsarukyan found an opening and fired an elbow.The first shot landed cleanly and appeared to knock Ruffy unconscious. Tsarukyan then delivered another elbow as his opponent fell, with referee Jason Herzog immediately stopping the contest at 4:56 of the first round.The finish made his earlier prediction look remarkably accurate. Tsarukyan had specifically mentioned elbows and cutting Ruffy’s face. Instead of needing three rounds to find the finish, he needed less than five minutes.There was also a funny twist involving N3on, who was part of Tsarukyan’s corner for the fight.After the knockout, Tsarukyan said the streamer had actually called for the elbow from the corner. “He called the elbow, I heard it, and I did it. Great cornerman… But we gotta change the color of his hair.”Tsarukyan’s win extended his winning streak to six fights and strengthened his position near the top of the UFC lightweight division. He also improved his professional record to 24-3 according to post-fight reports.Before the fight, Tsarukyan needed a statement performance. articles.title: Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua: Why Cardiff is winning race for long-awaited fight
articles.summary: Why Cardiff is set to beat competition from London and New York to host the long-awaited fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.
articles.body:
The long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua is expected to take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday, 11 December.

While BBC Sport understands final details are still being hammered out between Netflix, Saudi Arabian organisers Sela and both fighters' camps, Cardiff has firmly emerged as the frontrunner, with an official announcement expected this week.

It marks another dramatic twist in a saga that, only weeks ago, appeared destined for New York. A date at Madison Square Garden was so close to completion that plans were already being drawn up for a Manhattan news conference.

Instead, after Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to stage the fight on British soil, the Welsh capital has taken centre stage.

BBC Sport takes a look at how Cardiff became the leading candidate to host what would arguably be the biggest event in British boxing in the 21st Century.

Joshua and Matchroom stood firm on Britain

Wembley Stadium was long assumed to be the natural home for a meeting between the two defining British heavyweights of their generation. However, the path to making the fight was complicated by Joshua and Fury having signed separate agreements with Sela rather than a joint contract.

Joshua's deal explicitly stipulated that the bout must take place in the United Kingdom, whereas Fury's contained no such restriction.

That distinction proved critical when organisers and broadcast partner Netflix began lobbying to move the show to the United States.

Hearn acknowledged that virtually every other party involved preferred New York, with Matchroom even exploring what compensation would be required to waive the UK clause.

For a moment, that stand-off threatened to scupper the entire event. Fury publicly accused Joshua of stalling and briefly floated the prospect of a trilogy fight with Oleksandr Usyk.

But once Fury relented, organisers needed to find a British venue capable of satisfying the broadcast demands without leaving fans exposed to the British winter.

Cardiff, almost by process of elimination, became the answer.

The fight had initially been discussed for November but, with negotiations over the venue dragging on, it now looks set for December.

Staging an open-air stadium fight in the UK at that time carries immense risk.

While Wembley offers unmatched prestige, exposing tens of thousands of fans and a massive international broadcast operation to potentially freezing temperatures, wind and rain was deemed unacceptable.

Moving the event indoors to an arena like London's O2 would eliminate weather risks, but at the cost of sacrificing tens of thousands of ticket sales.

The Principality Stadium's retractable roof allows organisers to capture the immense scale, atmosphere and gate revenue of a stadium show while offering full protection from the elements.

The venue's official seated capacity is just under 74,000, but boxing configurations allow for even larger crowds.

Joshua has already proven he can sell out the venue, having defended his WBA and IBF titles there against Carlos Takam in front of nearly 80,000 fans in 2017 before adding the WBO belt against Joseph Parker five months later.

We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor

Fury says he is looking for new opponent, calls out Usyk

'Bring it on' - Cardiff businesses react to Fury vs Joshua rumours

A US-friendly start time is easier to accommodate

Perhaps the most difficult hurdle has been aligning the event with Netflix's preference to broadcast during prime-time hours in the United States.

A projected UK ring walk of about 01:00 GMT - 20:00 on the US east coast - created a logistical headache for London. Wembley operates under a strict 23:00 event curfew.

While Mayor of London Sadiq Khan offered his support and Wembley officials were open to discussions, securing the necessary approvals from Brent Council and local safety advisory groups for a 01:00 start presented an administrative hurdle.

Cardiff offers a far smoother path. The Welsh Rugby Union, which owns and operates the Principality Stadium, previously indicated it would be delighted to host the fight and confirmed a late-night finish would not be a dealbreaker.

While early-hours finishes still require extensive coordination around transport, policing and crowd management in the city centre, the venue already holds a clear precedent for late-night boxing. In 2007, Joe Calzaghe's super-middleweight unification victory over Mikkel Kessler did not start until 02:00 local time to satisfy American television network Showtime.

For all the delays and frustrations that have plagued this rivalry over the past decade, Fury against Joshua remains the pinnacle of domestic boxing. Downgrading to an indoor arena would diminish the magnitude of the occasion.

Crucially, taking the fight to America would have deprived domestic fans of a generational spectacle. British supporters have driven the commercial value of this rivalry for years, filling stadiums for both fighters' respective careers and following every collapsed negotiation.

Staging the bout on home soil serves as a long-overdue reward for that loyalty, even if both men are now former world heavyweight champions.

A stadium fight of this magnitude dominates the national conversation in a way a 04:00 New York or Las Vegas broadcast simply cannot, and local amateur boxing clubs could see a surge in interest when the country's biggest stars compete on home soil.

Wales also has history of staging a huge fight between two British heavyweights: In 1993, Lennox Lewis defended his WBC title against Frank Bruno at Cardiff Arms Park - the venue that the Principality Stadium replaced.

When the demands surrounding the event are broken down, Cardiff's emergence becomes easier to understand.

articles.title: Colby Covington takes u-turn on potential Khamzat Chimaev RAF wrestling match after preferring Kamaru Usman trilogy, says “I’d break Khamzat, he has quitter tendencies”
articles.summary: MMA News: Colby Covington has made a bold claim about a potential wrestling match against Khamzat Chimaev. The former UFC star believes his cardio and relentles.
articles.body: Colby Covington has made a bold claim about a potential wrestling match against Khamzat Chimaev. The former UFC star believes his cardio and relentless pace would eventually break the former UFC middleweight champion. Covington has also accused Chimaev of having “quitter tendencies” and believes he can expose them in a wrestling contest.The matchup has become a major talking point in Real American Freestyle (RAF). Chimaev recently hinted that he could wrestle Covington in Abu Dhabi. Covington is open to the idea, but he has insisted that the bout must happen at 185 pounds. He now believes Chimaev’s physical style would not be enough to deal with his pace.Will Colby Covington break Khamzat Chimaev in a wrestling match?Colby Covington has no doubts about how he would approach a potential wrestling match with Khamzat Chimaev. He believes the key would be his cardio.The former UFC welterweight title challenger has built his wrestling career around a high-pressure style. He constantly pushes the pace and looks to make his opponents work. Covington believes that could become a major advantage against Chimaev.“I think I would break Khamzat. He doesn’t have the cardio to keep up with me. He has those quitter tendencies. I will bring those quitter tendencies out of him if that’s the next matchup”, he told Submission Radio.Covington’s comments come as interest in a potential RAF showdown continues to grow. Chimaev recently appeared to reveal that the two could meet in Abu Dhabi.Covington believes that difference could become important if they meet under freestyle wrestling rules.The former UFC fighter has also made it clear that the weight would need to be agreed upon before the matchup can happen. He does not want to move into the 200-pound range to face Chimaev.Covington wants the contest at 185 pounds.Chimaev’s name is not the only one on Covington’s list. After his RAF 13 victory over Belal Muhammad, Covington said he would actually prefer a wrestling trilogy against Kamaru Usman.“You know, it’s, it’s a long list of guys, you know, and, and thankfully, you know, RAF has so much good talent for me to really challenge and test myself. But, you know, of course, you know, the Marty Fake Newsman, we have unfinished business. You know, that trilogy is a huge matchup. So, you know, that’s probably the top of the list”, he said.Covington and Usman previously fought twice in the UFC. Usman won both contests. He stopped Covington at UFC 245 in 2019 before defeating him by unanimous decision at UFC 268 in 2021.Covington has continued to dispute those results and sees wrestling as a chance to renew the rivalry under different rules.However, Chimaev remains a major option. Covington has previously named several other potential RAF opponents, including Gilbert Burns, Michael Chandler, Sean Brady and Arman Tsarukyan.For now, a Chimaev matchup is still dependent on the promotion finalising the details.
